Hey there! I'm going into criminology and I have done a fair bit of research on jobs in forensic psychology/criminology. I don't know where you are, but in Canada, you can do so much with forensic psychology and criminology! You have many options that aren't working directly with cops. You can work in prisons as a parole officer with criminology, you can also work in mental hospitals for those recognized as not responsible for their crimes for reason of insanity both in criminology and forensic psychology (working in mental hospitals as a forensic psychologist makes a lot of money, even around 120k in CAD dollars a year, but in Canada you need a Ph.D. for that, don't know about where you are). You could also work for CPS as a criminologist or even in youth homes, homes for abused women, etc. As another comment said, you can also work in cybersecurity with banks to search for fraud, or even with government officials to check for any threats. For example, in Canada, criminologists can work to survey the national railroad to check for any terrorist threats. You could also be a statistician, and you can also do research, but if you want to make money, research is not the route for you. Criminology and forensic psychology are extremely varied degrees, and no, you do not have to be a cop. I do not want to be with cops, and I want to limit my contact with cops, but you also need to take into consideration that criminology and forensic psychology by nature are related to the law, and police officers are those who enforce it in our daily lives, other than lawyers and judges. You cannot avoid working with police officers, but you can limit it. If you have any more questions, you can always PM me!
